title: Audit-family critique: which are load-bearing, and what the staleness metric actually measures
description: Filed as P8 during the W4 gate ("needs Jordan's call on which audit families are load-bearing"); this is the evidence for that call. Document: audit/2026-07-30-audit-family-critique/00_critique.md. HEADLINE. The vector audit IS the thing that identifies what is missing and nothing else in the repo computes it, AND its findings are near-stationary. Both are true at once and the staleness metric conflates them. MEASURED: over 8 days and 240 files of in-scope churn the feed moved 3 rows out of 178, in the improving direction (isolates 9->7, sparse_context 16->15; implied_missing 35 and notional 100 byte-stable). A freshness warning on a stationary backlog measures the wrong axis -- it says 're-run a script' when the message should be '178 structural gaps have gone unworked'. RECOMMENDATION 1 is therefore to INVERT what it reports (backlog counts, not drift), NOT to demote it; an earlier draft of this analysis recommended demotion and that was wrong, for the reason the two-axis split in the document's section 1 gives (content value and staleness informativeness are uncorrelated here). PER-FAMILY: mechanics-index is the one to promote -- it has NO generator, so its drift is editorial debt no script can clear, and it is the smallest number on the banner. vector-audit is highest on content value, lowest on staleness informativeness (both production paths regenerate the feed immediately before consuming it). graph-lexicon is low on both. decisions/proposals/apparatus are the governance observatory, NOT part of the vectorization review at all -- only vector-audit (its output), graph-lexicon (soft input) and mechanics-index (cited input) touch skills/valoria-vector-audit/. npc-audit should be reclassified: its artifact is an AUTHORED document, so 'stale' means a human must re-audit, sharing no remedy with 're-run a script'. THREE METRIC DEFECTS. D1: drift is computed from the artifact's last git COMMIT, not its last regeneration, so a no-op regen commits nothing and drift accumulates forever while the artifact is provably current -- not firing today (regeneration does change content) but silent when it does. D2: the weekly cron is nominally weekly, actually 1-in-3 -- exactly ONE scheduled refresh has ever landed (4029870, PR #244, 2026-07-27), the only commit matching the bot's own message; vector-audit and graph-lexicon last moved 07-22 and were not updated by the 07-27 run. D3: scope over-breadth manufactures the headline -- vector-audit's scope is most of the repo, so 240 files of churn produced 3 changed rows; the code carries a prior correction for exactly this failure mode at a smaller scope. THREE OF THIS ANALYSIS'S OWN HYPOTHESES WERE WRONG and were corrected by reading rather than grepping: ci_naming_check does NOT consume lexicon.json (it EXCLUDES it, skip-list at :70); review_core does NOT read apparatus_registry.yaml (comment only, :52); and the graph.json-pinned CI drift guard described at vector_audit.py:1215-1222 NO LONGER EXISTS -- the guard was rewritten to remove the dependency, so that docstring is STALE (recorded, not fixed: it is a skills/ file and this was a read-only critique). title: Standing gate: an adversarial steelmanned read-only review after EVERY milestone, not at the end
description: RULED (Jordan, 2026-08-04): 'use Fable 5 after every milestone/step to do an adversarial steelman read-only review for accuracy and logic and fidelity to plan'. Recorded in systems/_architecture/repository_keep_set_v1.md section 7.1 as a gate on every step of the evacuation sequence: a step is not complete until the review has run and its findings are applied or explicitly refused with a reason. WHAT THIS ADDS TO EXISTING DOCTRINE. CLAUDE.md section 10 already requires the agonist->antagonist relay and already wires valoria-critic (Read/Grep/Glob only, so independence is structural rather than declared, ED-IN-0087). It does NOT specify a CADENCE. This does: per MILESTONE, not per programme. JUSTIFIED FROM THIS PROGRAMME'S OWN RECORD, not from principle. Three defects in the separation work were found by adversarial passes and by nothing else, each invisible to the instrument that had just been built and pronounced sound: (1) the contest-groundup parity oracle sat in the evacuate set while a kept tool loads it to regenerate a committed golden a kept CI test asserts on (ED-IN-0130); (2) readers() could not see split paths, so the blocking-reader counts that sequence the entire deletion were blind to os.path.join construction -- 45 readers missed (ED-IN-0130); (3) deprecated/ holds 26 files of the BLOCKING ED-citation gate's universe, so the evacuation commit would have turned that gate red and the tempting fix would have destroyed the repo's only anti-fabrication check (ED-IN-0131). Each was cheap to check and expensive to have acted on. A single end-of-programme review would have caught all three AFTER the work they invalidate. THREE PROPERTIES THE GATE MUST KEEP or it decays into ceremony: (a) read-only BY CONSTRUCTION -- route through valoria-critic, never a prompt that merely declares read-only, since a sentence inside a prompt restricts nothing; (b) STEELMAN FIRST -- the reviewer states the strongest case for the work before attacking it, and 'this is correct and here is the best argument for it' is a valid verdict; (c) THE REVIEWER'S CLAIMS ARE CHECKED TOO -- reviews have been wrong in this programme (one reported id_reservations next_free unbumped when it was bumped; it had read a mid-session snapshot), so an audit is evidence, not a verdict. NOT YET ENFORCED. This is a convention with no guard. A CI check cannot observe whether a review ran, so the honest options are a per-step artifact under audit/ or a required line in the step's commit message. Filed rather than asserted -- per CLAUDE.md 0.1 point 5, if the guard cannot be written the pattern is not yet understood, and I am not claiming enforcement I have not built.

description: W2 of the ED-IN-0132-gated work list. Closes the stale surfaces the read-only state review found, and adds the guard that stops the largest one recurring. (1) THE KEEP-SET DOC DISAGREED WITH ITS OWN TOOL. repository_keep_set_v1.md:144,:151 still stated the superseded 2026-07-21 cutoff a full day after Jordan widened the window to 2026-07-01 (ED-IN-0129) -- so the doc and the partition-of-record disagreed about the rule deciding ~500 files. :157 still listed workplans/ and dashboard/ as evacuating when BOTH are kept, and the §4 banner still carried counts from two revisions ago (3146 -> 1149/6/1991) plus an 'unresolved coupling' that keeping workplans/ had already CLOSED. All corrected; the banner now says outright not to quote a count from the document. (2) THE FALSIFIER, because prose corrections have none. test_keep_set_doc_cutoff_matches_the_tool parses every `audit/` row in the doc that carries a comparison and asserts the ISO dates equal evacuation_plan.AUDIT_CUTOFF. MUTATION-VERIFIED: reverting the constant to 2026-07-21 turns it red; restored byte-exact; 29 tests green. This is the two-surfaces-drift failure the programme keeps hitting -- CARRY/LEAVE vs the tree, a proposal vs the manifest, this doc vs the tool -- and a prose fix without a guard only resets the clock until the next ruling. (3) THE FORK PLAN'S TWO RESIDUALS. :350-352 still posed C7 as live ('Only Jordan can answer that') while §9 had struck it; now carries a do-not-reopen banner citing the D1 ruling and PP-233's simultaneity implementation, with the original preserved as the record of the error. :433 still asserted present-tense that each C-item 'is filed as its own ED' -- the exact defect this document prosecutes in ED-IN-0124(f). Corrected with what actually happened, which is better: all eight were RULED on 2026-08-04 and registered collectively (ED-IN-0125, plus ED-MB-0064 for C2's MB content), so per-item needs_jordan EDs would now double-register settled decisions. The forcing mechanism was not needed because the ruling arrived first. (4) A HAND-MAINTAINED COUNT IN THE LOADER FOR THE FILE IT PARSES. engine/substrate/keys.py:14,:183 described a '44-type roster'. VERIFIED against three independent sources: the registry has 55 `### ` headings, tools/build_key_graph.py:7 says 55, and TypeRegistry.load() itself returns 55 types. The loader's docstring was wrong about the file it loads, by 11. Corrected to 55. This is the same duplicate-of-a-derivable class as the 4 hand-made .tres key-type resources, and it argues for W4 (the registry inversion) rather than for more careful hand-editing.
